selfMeasurementContract.rule: EVERY figure published in this file is exactly one of: (1) a CENSUS figure -- a property of the emitted bytes, computed at the fixed point described below and re-verified against the file on disk after the final write; (2) a DERIVED count -- the length of a list or table that is itself published in this file, stated next to a pointer naming what to recount; or (3) a PROCESS FACT -- a measurement of this pass's generation run (assertion tallies, checker exits) that is NOT recomputable from the file and is labelled as such where it appears. selfMeasurementContract.theFixedPoint: serialise the COMPLETE object; parse the serialised bytes through the duplicate-key-rejecting hook; walk every leaf and key, classifying bool-before-int; write the census figures into the object; repeat until two consecutive serialisations are byte-identical; write; re-read from disk; walk again and assert every published census figure true of the disk bytes. injectivityByInverse.claim: the encoding of every record type in this artifact is INJECTIVE ON LOGICAL VALUES, so two different logical values cannot produce one preimage.

proofInTWOSteps.STEP-1-THE-FRAMING-IS-INJECTIVE: A TOTAL DECODER is exhibited: for each record type it reads the record tag, then for each declared field in declared order reads uint8(tag), uint32be(len) and exactly len bytes, and RAISES on a tag mismatch, a length that overruns the buffer, a missing field, or any trailing byte. decode(encode(x)) recovers the exact ordered list of FIELD BYTE STRINGS for every x in the accepted domain.
proofInTWOSteps.STEP-2-THE-VALUE-TO-BYTES-MAP-IS-INJECTI: step 1 alone does NOT reach the claim, because it inverts the framing and not the value encoding. The second step rests on two rules stated above and is now folded into the argument rather than left beside it: (a) TEXT is REJECTED rather than normalized when not already NFC, so no two distinct accepted strings share a UTF-8 encoding; (b) INTEGERS are canonicalUnsignedDecimal under ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$, so no two distinct accepted integers share a byte string and no integer has two accepted spellings. Composing the two steps, encode has a left inverse on logical values, so encode is injective, so H(encode(x)) collides only if SHA-256 does.
proofInTWOSteps.REPAIREDINV2: v1's argument stopped at step 1 and stated the step-2 conclusion. The conclusion was correct -- the review verified it empirically and so did this author -- but the stated proof did not reach it. This is the review's N-1 and it is repaired by making the second step explicit, not by changing any rule.

injectivityByInverse.whatThisMakesInexpressible: the concatenation ambiguity where ('ab','c') and ('a','bc') share a preimage. It is not a case to be listed and guarded; it has no representation, because each component carries its own explicit length before its bytes and the field boundary set is therefore a function of the byte string alone.
injectivityByInverse.executed: the decoder was run against records encoded for the vectors in this artifact, including the full 13-field SemanticEvidenceV1 of ED-1 and the nested RawProofInventoryV1 recovered from its 0x9a field, and the round trip was asserted each time.
injectivityByInverse.domainOfInjectivity: records, and SETS of records. The set commitment of R-0 is DELIBERATELY not injective on sequences: any permutation of the same record set yields the same digest, which is the point. Under the reject-duplicates rule adopted here, a sequence with a repeat has no image at all, so a multiset cannot be expressed and cannot collide with the set that underlies it. See divergencesFound.DIV-1. AND THE NON-ASCII DOMAIN IS NOW EXERCISED: BND-5 pins the NFC-unstable singleton class and BND-6 separates NFC from NFKC, so the two normalization-shaped ways to lose injectivity are both falsifiable rather than argued. v2's reviewer attacked this region and found no collision; v3 turns that finding into vectors so the next implementation is checked rather than trusted.

typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.rule: NO TEST VECTOR IN THIS ARTIFACT CAN ENFORCE LAW 18, AND NONE CLAIMS TO.
typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.why: a digest cannot police the JSON type of its input. An implementation that admits schemaVersion 1.0 and coerces it to the integer 1 before encoding produces the CORRECT canonicalUnsignedDecimal byte 0x31 and therefore the CORRECT digest. The vector passes and law 18 has been violated. Only an admission gate placed BEFORE encoding can catch it, which is exactly what section 6 law 18 says: 'Deriving an identity, ref, commitment, or fingerprint from an admission-stage record that has not passed this gate is forbidden.'
typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.andItGENERALISES: the same argument defeats a vector at EVERY scalar position in every recipe -- a boolean coerced to an enum text, a numeric string coerced to an integer, an integer-valued float in the inventory schemaVersion. The mechanism is named rather than the instances, which is why no additional exposure hides behind the narrower phrasing.
typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.consequence: these recipes are defined ONLY over records that have already passed exact-type admission. A conforming implementation must reject a boolean, a float or a numeric string where an unsigned integer is declared, and must reject a non-string where text is declared, before it computes anything here. This artifact declares that precondition and does not test it.

parameters.recordType: which record grammar the items use
parameters.domain: the closed domain label placed in the outer frame

steps: 1. ADMIT. Every item has already passed exact-type admission (sharedPrimitives.typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob) and every text component satisfies sharedPrimitives.textComponent INCLUDING the <=4096-byte bound and the closed-ASCII-grammar clause. An item that has not is not an input.
2. ENCODE. Each item becomes its complete record byte string under its declared recordType.
3. CANONICALISE THE SET. Sort the complete record byte strings, unsigned bytewise lexicographic, ASCENDING. Duplicates: see duplicateRule.

4. LEAF. leafHash(r) = SHA-256( 0x00 || uint64be(byteLength(r)) || r ). Note uint64be here, NOT the uint32be of the component frame. This is the grammar's leafLength rule and getting it wrong is the single easiest way to produce a plausible wrong digest.

5. FOLD. While more than one node remains, pair adjacent nodes left to right: internalHash(l, r) = SHA-256( 0x01 || l || r ), each of l and r being exactly 32 raw bytes. ODD NODE: if a level has an odd count, the FINAL node is PROMOTED UNCHANGED to the next level. It is NOT duplicated and NOT paired with itself.

6. EMPTY SET. If the item set is empty there is no leaf and no fold. root = SHA-256( 0x02 || C(0x30, UTF8(namespace)) ). Note this preimage carries the NAMESPACE and NOT the domain -- see observations.OBS-3, which is a real consequence.
7. OUTER FRAME. preimage = 0x30 || C(0x31, UTF8(namespace)) || C(0x32, ASCII(domain)) || C(0x33, root32bytes). commitment = 'sha256:' || lowerhex(SHA-256(preimage)).
R-0-typedComponentMerkleSet.whatTheOUTERFRAMEDOESNOTBIND: the leaf count N. The preimage is recordTag, namespace, domain and root, and nothing else. N is not an input at any position. This is harmless for INJECTIVITY -- measured in this pass, 301 distinct roots for N=0..300 with 0 collisions, and the v3 reviewer independently measured the same range with the same result -- and it is NOT harmless for any proof that needs to know the leaf list is complete. See correctionsOfRecord.WD-3.theMEASUREDOBSTACLE and observations.OBS-4.

orderingRule.sortedByWhat: THE COMPLETE ITEM RECORD BYTES. Not the logical field values, not the subject text, not any Unicode collation, not insertion order, not producer order.
orderingRule.underWhichComparison: unsigned bytewise lexicographic, ascending. Byte values are compared as integers 0..255. A prefix sorts before any string extending it.
orderingRule.theConsequenceMOSTIMPLEMENTATIONSWILLGET: because every record begins with a fixed record tag and every text field is preceded by uint32be(length), the induced order is LENGTH-MAJOR within a field, THEN content. For single-field records the order over subject strings is: shorter UTF-8 first, and only then bytewise. So 'b' sorts BEFORE 'aa', which is the OPPOSITE of sorting the subject strings. Vectors UC-4 and SS-4 pin both digests so a wrong implementation is identified rather than merely failed.
orderingRule.isOrderDefinedByTheSetOrByInsertion: BY THE SET. Insertion order is not an input and cannot be recovered from the commitment. Vector ED-4 demonstrates this at the inventory layer: the same three items supplied in declared and reversed order yield one identical EvidenceDigest.
orderingRule.whyOrderAtAll: SO THAT THE MAP FROM A SET OF RECORDS TO A BYTE STRING IS A FUNCTION. Without a total order on records the set has no canonical serialization and two honest producers disagree. THE SORT HAS EXACTLY ONE FURTHER JOB IN THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN CONSTRUCTION, AND v2 DISCLAIMED IT: it puts duplicates ADJACENT, which is what makes the adopted REJECT rule of duplicateRule decidable in a single pass. Step 3 says 'CANONICALISE THE SET ... Duplicates: see duplicateRule', and evidence.v10#recordRules.sets states the two operations in that order -- sort, then reject. This author's encoder detects duplicates by adjacent comparison on the sorted sequence and raises 'duplicate exact record bytes'. THE SORT IS NOT CLAIMED TO ENABLE NON-MEMBERSHIP PROOFS from adjacent-leaf paths -- that rationale belongs to evidence.v1's different construction, R-4 does not adopt it, and it remains WITHDRAWN. See correctionsOfRecord.WD-3 and understatementsCorrected.U-2.

duplicateRule.statement: a repeated exact record byte string is an ERROR. The producer is refused and NO digest is defined for that input.
duplicateRule.why: under the alternative -- silently deduplicate -- the input sequences [a,a,b] and [a,b] map to ONE commitment while the surrounding record can independently declare a cardinality. evaluation-proof.v8's own no-match proof carries subjectCount as a separate field that the Merkle root does not bind (observations.OBS-4). So a producer could declare subjectCount 3 over the subject multiset [a,a,b] and commit to the root of the 2-element set, and the commitment would verify. REJECT makes that input inexpressible rather than detectable.
duplicateRule.THISISADEPARTUREFromOneClauseOfOneSource: evaluation-proof.v8 says DEDUPLICATE in two places; evidence.v10 says REJECT; and evaluation-proof.v8's OWN recordRules.duplicates says duplicates are FORBIDDEN. This artifact adopts REJECT, which is faithful to evidence.v10 AND to evaluation-proof.v8's recordRules, and dissents only from evaluation-proof.v8's two deduplicate clauses. Vector SS-5 publishes the digest under BOTH rules so the choice is visible and falsifiable. See divergencesFound.DIV-1.

domainSeparation.mechanism: the domain occupies a LENGTH-FRAMED component at a FIXED ordinal of the outer preimage, tagged 0x32, between the namespace and the root.
domainSeparation.propertyRatherThanList: there is no rule of the form 'digest X may appear only at position Y' to enumerate, keep in sync and get wrong. A digest computed under domain D simply IS NOT the digest under domain D-prime: the preimages differ in a length-framed slot, so equality requires a SHA-256 collision. Vector OC-6 pins this by committing one identical record set under 'outcome-set' and under 'universe' and publishing both digests. The review extended this to all nine domains over one identical root and obtained nine distinct commitments.
domainSeparation.whyLengthFramedAndNotAPrefix: a bare prefix admits a boundary slide: domain 'abc' with payload 'd' and domain 'ab' with payload 'cd' share a byte string. The 4-byte length before the domain makes that impossible. Vector ED-6 pins the same argument for the EVIDENCE envelope, with both full preimage hexes.

nodeTypeSeparation.rule: leaf preimages begin 0x00, internal preimages begin 0x01, the empty-set preimage begins 0x02, the outer preimage begins 0x30. All four are distinct at byte 0.
nodeTypeSeparation.consequence: a leaf hash can never be an internal hash and a single-element root can never be an empty-set root, so the classic second-preimage attack that promotes an internal node into a leaf position has no preimage available. This is why PROMOTE UNCHANGED is safe here where a bare unprefixed Merkle would need duplicate-last or a length commitment.
nodeTypeSeparation.andThereforeTheTreeShapeIsDetermined: given the leaf count N the pairing schedule is fixed, and given node-type separation the root determines the ordered leaf list up to SHA-256 collision. Cardinality does not need a separate commitment FOR INJECTIVITY. It IS needed for any proof of completeness or adjacency, which is a different property and is not claimed here.

theRelation.name: SUBJECT-INCLUSION-VERIFY-V1 (candidate)
inputs: commitment: a TCMS-V5 outer commitment string, sha256:<64 lowercase hex>
domain: the closed domain label the consumer REQUIRES the commitment to be under (for subject sets: 'subject-set')
record: the complete candidate item record bytes (for subject sets: a SubjectV1 record)
path: a sequence of steps, each a pair (side, siblingHash) with side in {sibling-on-left, sibling-on-right} and siblingHash exactly 32 bytes
algorithm: 1. ADMIT the record: it must decode under its declared record grammar and every text component must satisfy sharedPrimitives.textComponent, including the 4096-byte bound and reject-not-normalize. A record that fails admission verifies nothing.
3. for each step in path order: x := SHA-256(0x01 || siblingHash || x) when side is sibling-on-left, else SHA-256(0x01 || x || siblingHash).
4. ACCEPT iff 'sha256:' || lowerhex(SHA-256(0x30 || C(0x31, UTF8(namespace)) || C(0x32, ASCII(domain)) || C(0x33, x))) equals the commitment, byte for byte.
theRelation.everyConstantIsRZeroTranscribed: the four preimage prefixes 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x30, the outer frame tags 0x31/0x32/0x33, uint64be leaf length and 32-byte node width are all R-0's transcribed rules; this relation introduces NO new constant, tag, domain string or hash. F-1-subjectInclusionVerification.whatAcceptanceEstablishes: under SHA-256 collision resistance: the record is a member of the committed set -- i.e. it was one of the sorted leaf records folded into the commitment's root, under the commitment's own namespace and the domain the CONSUMER supplied. Node-type separation carries the argument: a leaf preimage begins 0x00 with a uint64be length, an internal preimage begins 0x01 at fixed 65-byte width, the empty-set preimage begins 0x02, and the outer preimage begins 0x30 -- so no accepted fold can conflate a record with an internal node, an empty root, or another domain's commitment. Vectors IP-NEG-1 through IP-NEG-5 exercise each refusal.
whatAcceptanceDoesNOTEstablish: the set's CARDINALITY -- the outer frame does not bind N (R-0.whatTheOUTERFRAMEDOESNOTBIND), and a path proves one membership, not a count
the record's POSITION or the path's uniqueness -- position is not an input to the relation and is not recoverable from it
NON-MEMBERSHIP of anything -- a completeness/adjacency claim needs N bound to the commitment, which this construction does not do; ESC-08's non-membership encoding remains open and untouched
that the COMMITMENT ITSELF is the right one -- which commitment a consumer must check against is the surrounding contract's job (DUD-3), not the relation's
anything about an EMPTY commitment -- the empty root is not a leaf hash and no path verifies against it (IP-NEG-5)

This is WD-3's measured obstacle made executable, and any future wire encoding must carry variable-length paths.
F-1-subjectInclusionVerification.proverNote: INFORMATIVE. A prover holding the full sorted leaf-record list derives the path for index i by walking the fold: at each level, if i is even and i+1 exists the step is (sibling-on-right, hash at i+1); if i is odd the step is (sibling-on-left, hash at i-1); if i is the promoted final node there is NO step; then i := floor(i/2). This note describes one way to produce a path and binds nothing; the relation above is the contract.
